tasks.title: A pin is judged on the copy the session will load, and a step that stops gives back nothing a pending decision or an outstanding dispatch holds - the lock and the task's start included
tasks.description:
An independent review of the two tasks before this one (the orchestrator's prompt names its file; every finding below was RUN unless it says by reading, and its probes sit beside it) found two med defects and several lows of ONE class - the task before this one set out to make a stopped step write nothing the next step reads, and the review found writes it did not reach. This is the second time the class has come back, so the fix is the invariant held by a derived case, not the list of places.

WHAT THE REVIEW SHOWED.
(1) med - THE LOCK. `lock_to_give_back` returns true on any stop before it looks at `pending`, so a stopped `--answer resume` keeps the decision (the task before this one's fix) and gives the phase lock back anyway. Another session's `next` then takes the phase (exit 0) and the first session's same answer is refused: 'HELD by a live run -- another-session'. With the decision pending and no stop, the other session is refused. `drive`'s docstring promises the lock is kept while a decision is pending or a dispatch is out; the paragraph the task before this one added to PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md says the opposite. The same rule shows in a wave: a stop prints 'lock released' while an earlier member's executor is out.
(2) med - THE COPY THAT IS JUDGED IS NOT THE COPY THAT IS LOADED. On the session route the drive's pre-check (`session_skills`, `session_hand`, `ask_member_pins`) hashes the skill in the PROJECT, while each wave member's session loads the copy in its own tree, cut from HEAD, and the runner checks that tree. Restoring the bytes in the project without committing - which is what the stop's remedy says to do - passes the pre-check, both members are marked, the runner exits 2 naming the tree's path, and the next `next` treats a session that never started as one with no result. No race is needed. Rooted in the pin's own task; the same at both later commits. On the subagent route the brief also judges the project's copy while the member's tree holds the changed bytes; which copy a subagent's Skill tool loads is Claude Code's and could not be run.
(3) low - A SERIAL STEP STARTS THE TASK BEFORE IT ASKS. A single task stopped over a pin has gone pending -> in_progress, attempts 0 -> 1, startedAt set; the wave path asks before starting anything. The previous task's title promised the plan's state.
(4) low - the shape-2 warning is dropped from the `--signal` line the main loop reads (`+1`, exit 0) on each step while an earlier member still prints; it surfaces only once nothing else is due.
(6) low - `review_fix_dispatch` builds its command from the pre-check's read but no case holds it (dropping `held=hand` stays green), and it runs after the mark and can still stop, against `dispatch`'s docstring 'a dispatch that stops has marked nothing'.
(7) low - `validation_dispatch` writes its prompt before it asks the pins: a stop leaves an orphan prompt file.
(9) low - the pre-check's stop ends the step for every member, so a member whose executor returned waits on another member's skill. That is the rule as written; the `owes_executor` docstring overclaims.
(10) low BY READING - a wave member's pinned directory is hashed up to three times in the opening step; 'one read per step' holds only from `dispatch` to the command.
(11) low - `resume_writer(consume=False)`: one caller, always true; the default is a branch nothing takes.
(5, the drive's half) low - mutations that left the suite green: four `owes_executor` branches (parked, not ready, stale brief, proof held) though PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE cites spd17 for two of them; `break` -> `continue` after a shape-2 stop.

THE RULE TO BUILD. Two invariants, each held by ONE derived case rather than a case per place.
A. A STEP THAT STOPS HAS WRITTEN NOTHING THE NEXT STEP READS - AND THE PLAN AND THE LOCK ARE PART OF WHAT IT READS. Widen the kept-state snapshot of the task before this one (`_kept_state` in tests/test_drive_phase.py) to the plan's task fields the drive reads (status, attempts, startedAt, the dispatch-relevant notes) and the lock's holder, and compare it whole before and after EVERY pin stop the drive can reach: single task on each route, wave member first and second on each route, resume, review-fix, the phase-level validation prompt. Derive the list of stop routes from the code (every call that can raise `PinStop` or return a pin stop, the way spd1 derives hand-out callers), so a stop route added later without a row is red by name. Where the comparison cannot be whole for a reason (a journal row recording the stop is a record, not state; the lock released because NOTHING is pending and nothing is out is correct), the case states the exception with its reason, and the exceptions are a short table checked in both directions. Concretely the code then must: keep the lock on a stop while a decision is pending or a dispatch is out (the usage arm already does this - one rule, not two); ask a serial task's pins before `start_task`, as the wave does; ask `review_fix_dispatch`'s and `validation_dispatch`'s pins before any mark or write. If a write genuinely cannot move ahead of its stop, the stop says what it left and the next step reads it correctly - say which and why.
B. A PIN IS JUDGED ON THE COPY THAT WILL BE LOADED. On the session route that is the member's tree: before a tree exists, judge the commit the trees will be cut from (the skill directory's bytes at that commit, read from git without a checkout, for a project-level skill inside the repository; a personal or plugin skill lies outside the cut and its on-disk copy is the copy loaded); once a tree exists, judge the tree. The stop's remedy then names what to do for THAT copy ('restore the bytes and commit them' when the copy is a commit's). On the subagent route state, in the code and in SECURITY.md's pinned-skill section, which copy the brief judges and that which copy the Skill tool then loads is Claude Code's - do not claim more. Decide whether a working-tree copy that differs from HEAD for a project skill should itself be a stop or a warning on the serial session route (the session there also runs in a tree cut from HEAD? read where a single task's session runs before deciding) and say why.
C. The lows that are not the class: fix (4) so the main loop's signal line carries the warning; reword (9)'s docstring to what the rule is; remove (11)'s dead default or give it a caller; (10) is a cost to state in a docstring, not to fix, unless B's change removes it. The missing cases of (5): make each branch of `owes_executor` and the `break` able to fail, each with its allow twin.

ALLOW CASES: everything the task before this one held stays green line for line (a wave whose pins match, a plan with no pins, a matching resume); a stop while nothing is pending and nothing is out still gives the lock back; a personal skill pinned and unchanged on disk dispatches; a project skill committed with the pinned bytes dispatches even when the working copy is being edited, if B decides the commit is the copy loaded.

HOW TO PROVE. (1) high, a regression, fails closed - `skills_at_commit` reads a commit's skill directory from `git ls-tree`/`cat-file` and refuses what a checkout reads: a skill directory that is a committed link (`.claude/skills/x -> ../../vendor/x`) is refused, and a `.claude/skills` that is itself a link picks nothing ('no copy is found'). A submodule entry is the same root: a checkout reads an empty directory and digests it; the commit reader refuses. Probe link_probe.py L1/L2 on the real `next`, commit_probe.py c1/c6.
(2) med - `_stop_route_functions` counts a function as a stop route only when its OWN body calls one of a fixed list of names. tasks.description:
The task before this one made `meta.skillPins` stop a session over a skill whose directory is not the pinned bytes. Nothing yet WRITES a pin except a hand edit of the plan, nothing tells a user which of the plan's skills are pinned and whether they still match, and nothing says how an outside skill becomes a project skill in the first place. Read that task's reader and digest in `_skill_places.py` before anything else; this task adds no second reading of a pin.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A VERB WRITES THE PIN, under the manifest lock, with a journal row, revalidating through validate-manifest.py like every verb that mutates the plan: `/audit:task skill-pin <name> [--source <text>]` pins the directory digest of the copy the resolver finds NOW and prints the path and the digest it pinned; `--remove --reason <text>` drops one. It refuses, writing nothing, for a name the resolver cannot place or a directory with no digest, and it says when the copy it is about to pin is a personal one (a home directory no clone carries - the pin would then fail on every other machine) and refuses that without an explicit flag whose name says so. Re-pinning a name that is pinned prints the old and the new digest. The verb is the one the plugin's command file routes to: `plugins/audit/commands/task.md` is at its context ceiling (`python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` prints it), so the verb's mention must fit under it by shortening something of equal standing, never by raising the ceiling; if it cannot fit, stop and say what would have to go.
2. THE DOCTOR READS IT BACK, read-only, in the row family that already answers whether the plan's skills resolve (`_doctor_policy.check_plan_skills`): for each pinned name - matches (path), does not match (path, both digests, and that a session naming it will not start), not found where its bytes can be read; a pin naming a skill nothing in the plan names any more (a warning: stale); and, when the plan pins at least one skill, the plan-named skills that are NOT pinned, by name, as information and not as a warning. A plan with no skillPins key gets no new row at all. A mismatch on THIS machine is a warning, never a finding that fails a build, for the reason that function's docstring already gives for a skill absent here.
3. ONE PAGE says how to vendor an outside skill, placed by the audience split CONTRIBUTING.md's decision record states (read it: the plugin's user-facing reference under plugins/audit/reference/, linked from the README's skills section - not a section of the README, not QUICKSTART). It states, each with the reason: copy the skill's directory into the project's `.claude/skills/<a name that says what it does and collides with nothing built in>`, never install the outside plugin for one skill; read the whole text before it is committed, since it is instructions an agent with a shell will follow; give it a `## Checklist` section, because a headless session is handed only the description and that section; take out any step that commits, pushes, spawns agents or fetches from the network, since the brief's rules win and a skill that asks for them only produces a conflict in the return; record where it came from (repository, commit, licence) beside it; pin it with the verb; and to upgrade - replace the directory, read the diff, re-pin. And what none of that buys: a pin proves the bytes, not that they are safe, and a skill being invoked is never evidence that its workflow was followed - the gates are.
4. The page claims nothing the code does not do: every sentence about behaviour names the verb or the row that does it (the before-you-claim skill's first question), and a pin over the page's own example commands is not needed.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER THIS TASK SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN (three tasks landed after the pin itself; read their text in docs/audit/phases/SG2.json, SG2.15-xk1, SG2.16-xk1 and SG2.17-xk1). The verb, the doctor and the page follow the reader as it now is, and restate none of it: (a) the digest is `_skill_places.skill_digest` - lstat before read, a non-regular entry or a link out makes the directory unreadable naming the entry, Markdown alone has CRLF read as LF, every entry counts including tool-written ones (`TOOL_WRITTEN`); the verb calls it and computes nothing of its own, and its refusal for 'a directory with no digest' prints the reader's own words (the entry and its kind). (b) A pin is about the directory a name resolves to, and two pins on one directory with different digests are a validation error: the verb pins under the spelling it is given, and re-pinning a directory already pinned under another spelling updates THAT pin or refuses naming it - never leaves two pins the validator then refuses (the verb revalidates, so the case is that the verb itself says which, before writing). (c) The doctor's 'not found where its bytes can be read' row has three answers to tell apart: not found, unreadable (the reader's words, naming the entry), and mismatch - which names a tool-written entry when one is present, as the runner's stop already does, by calling the same helper. On the session route a wave member's pin is judged on the copy its session loads (SG2.17-xk1): the doctor judges the project's working copy and says so, and when that copy differs from HEAD for a project skill it says the commit is what a wave's sessions will load. (d) The page's 'what a pin does not prove' is a pointer to SECURITY.md's pinned-skill section, not a copy of it; what the page owns is the vendoring steps, including that a checkout which converts line endings changes the digest of any file but Markdown, and the remedy (mark the skill directory as not text for git, with the one line of `.gitattributes` that does it), that a bytecode cache or `.DS_Store` written into the directory after pinning makes the pin mismatch, and that restored bytes must be committed before a wave's sessions see them.

ALLOW CASES: the doctor on a plan with no pins prints what it printed before; the verb on a matching, already pinned skill changes nothing and says so; `--remove` of a name that is not pinned refuses and changes nothing.

HOW TO PROVE. Red first for the verb's refusals and the doctor's three answers. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the verb pinning SKILL.md's digest instead of the directory's (the round trip verb -> reader must then mismatch); the verb skipping revalidation; the doctor's mismatch row printed as a match; the personal-copy refusal removed. The round trip is a case of its own: pin with the verb, then the reader of the previous task answers match; change one byte, it answers mismatch; re-pin, match. `python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate` green.

NOT in this task: any change to when a session stops (the previous task); the panel.

(2) The doctor names each pinned skill as matching, not matching or not found, a stale pin, and the unpinned plan skills, and prints nothing new for a plan with no pins.
(3) The command file mentions the verb and stays under its context ceiling.
(4) One reference page says how to vendor and pin a skill, linked from the README, with no sentence about behaviour the code does not do.

tasks.description:
An independent review of SG2.19-xk1 (the orchestrator's prompt names its directory; HOLD-1, probe alias_probe.py, outputs out/alias_new.txt and out/alias_old.txt; re-run by the orchestrator on fresh exports of both commits with the same result) found one regression a user sees.

WHAT HAPPENS. In the commit, `.claude/skills/alias-a` is a link to the pinned `vendored-a`, whose committed bytes are not the pinned ones; in the working copy `alias-a` was replaced, uncommitted, by a plain directory whose bytes match. A session-route wave member names `alias-a`. At fff769ee: exit 1 with the commit-form stop, P1.1 pending with attempts 0, no tree cut, drive state `{}`. At 9e0e4d3b: the step prints 'started P1.1; tree for P1.1', P1.1 is `in_progress` with attempts 1, the wave and its tree are recorded in state, a worktree is left registered, and only then does the walk stop in the member's tree. The cause (drive-phase.py:9887-9888, the `uncut` list, and :9901, `names_a_pin`): whether a member needs the commit's checkout is decided by `covering_pins` over the project's WORKING COPY, and a member left out of `uncut` is then asked with `where=None` - the working copy again - even when the step makes a checkout for another member (C2). So the decision reads one copy and the session loads another, which is the exact class SG2.17 closed for the judgment itself.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
A. The question 'does this member name a pinned skill' is asked of the same copy the judgment reads and the member's session will load: for an uncut session-route member, the commit. So no decision about the commit's copy reads the working copy. Keep SG2.19's properties: at most one checkout per commit per step; none for a plan with no pins or `skillPins: {}`; none when no uncut session-route member names any skill. If keeping 'no checkout when the names resolve to no pinned directory' needs the commit read anyway, drop that refinement rather than reading the working copy - say which and why, with the git-process count per wave-opening step before and after.
B. A step that stops over a pin after it has started a member or cut its tree gives back that start, that tree and its registration, and the wave record - the SG2.16/SG2.17 property, held by SG2.19's snapshot-at-the-stop rule. Add this scenario (the review's C1 and C2) to the stop scenarios that rule runs, so the snapshot sees it; if the snapshot rule did not reach it because no scenario did, say so in the case's label.

ALLOW CASES: working copy equal to the commit (C0, stops with nothing changed on both commits); a plan with no pins (zero git processes for the pin check, real `next` byte for byte as at 9e0e4d3b); a matching pin behind a committed link dispatching (as at 9e0e4d3b); a member whose tree is already cut is judged in that tree.

HOW TO PROVE. Red first on the tree as it stands with the review's alias_probe.py C1/C2 and a suite case per scenario; a mutation probe of your own (copies of the working tree, each mutation asserted applied, caches purged), each deny with its allow twin: the decision read from the working copy again; the stop's give-back skipped for a started member. SG2.19's mutation table (its directory) still answers as owed except rows whose code this changes - name each and why. The drive suite's touched block alone, then the whole suite once through the sweep with --jobs 4.

NOT in this task: the review's BATCH items (calls without a Call node, the private remedy name, the windows per-step cost sentence, the TMPDIR remedy) - they go to the phase's low batch.

Acceptance:
(1) Whether an uncut session-route member needs the commit's copy is decided over the commit, so a working copy that differs from the commit can neither skip a stop nor move it after the member's start.
(2) A step that stops over a pin after starting a member or cutting its tree leaves the plan, the state, the trees and git's worktree registrations as it found them, held by the snapshot-at-the-stop rule over this scenario.
